contract: Library and item scanning, file discovery, metadata precedence, watcher and cron wiring and metadata writing equivalent to upstream LibraryScanner/LibraryItemScanner/BookScanner/AudioFileScanner: discovery groups media files into items with the documented ignore rules, audio files carry probed fields and are ordered by disc/track with chapters offset by duration, item identity survives renames through the inode fallback, the precedence snapshot is applied and persisted, chunked items_added/items_updated events are filtered per user, metadata.json is written to metadata/items/<id>, scan counters count missing items on every scan while a podcast folder that still exists is exempt, and the watcher and the auto-scan cron each start scans on their own.

invariants.contract: Scan counters: a library scan reports one missing for an item folder that disappeared, reports the same missing count again on a later scan instead of clearing it, flags the row isMissing, clears the flag and counts one update when the folder returns, and reports zero missing for a podcast item whose folder still exists even when all its episode files are gone.

An item folder renamed in place is matched to the existing item by its unchanged folder inode: the scan keeps the item id, book id and ino, follows the new path and relPath, and keeps the title stored in the item's metadata.json.
exceptions: Reciprocal single-file inode matching (a library file ino matching another item's ino) is deliberately omitted by the Go rewrite and is recorded in its importGroup note; this packet pins the folder-rename and file-into-folder cases upstream implements.

invariants.contract: Audio files of a book carry the probed fields (path, ext, ext-derived format and codec, duration, ino) and are ordered by disc then track with 1-based index; a CD01/CD02 folder pair is one item ordered by disc; the book's chapters follow that order with ids 0..n-1 where start equals the cumulative duration of the preceding files and end equals start plus the file's probed duration (within 1e-6); a folder whose only audio file cannot be probed becomes no item.
exceptions: OverDrive MediaMarkers chapters cannot be produced from this pin's ffprobe JSON path (recorded limitation, not asserted).

invariants.contract: A book item that loses its only media file (its ebook) is flagged isMissing by the library scan, and a later scan after the file returns clears the flag.

Grouping adds a file item for a media file in a book library root, folds CD01/CD02 directories into the parent item, ignores dot files and dot directories, @eaDir directories, temporary extensions (.part and friends) and folders flagged by an .ignore file, and drops media files in a podcast library root entirely.
exceptions: Ebook-only items are grouped but not imported: owner-approved compatibility-stub exception (2026-10-30); ebook media classification and grouping stay in scope.

invariants.contract: A new podcast folder imports as one podcast item whose title comes from the album tag of its first episode file and whose episodes take title and publishedAt from the audio tags, later item scans add an episode for a copied audio file and delete the episode row of a deleted file, and a new book folder holding audio and an epub imports both with the epub as ebookFile.

The library's persisted metadataPrecedence is applied by a forced scan and re-persisted unchanged in extraData.lastScanMetadataPrecedence on every completed scan; with absMetadata first the folder title wins for title and authors while values only the sidecar supplied (series) remain; an item whose only media is an ebook takes the title and language that the parsed opf supplies from the parsed ebook metadata through the audioMetatags source (no audio file: the epub's dc:title overrides the folder title) while an author without an opf:role stays the folder-derived name, and a rescan keeps those values.

A scan that changes books emits items_added (new items) and items_updated (rescanned items) events whose payloads are arrays of expanded items (id and media.metadata.title) of at most ten items each, delivering every item exactly once, to every authenticated socket whose user can access the library, and to no socket of a user restricted to another library and to no unauthenticated socket; twelve updated items arrive as the chunks of ten and two.
exceptions: Series RSS-feed closure on a removed series is not wired to the Go RSS manager; the source-side feed closing is not asserted here.

invariants.contract: When a scan adds a book it writes metadata/items/<id>/metadata.json (and nothing into the item folder while storeMetadataWithItem is off) with the item's values, and that file is not part of the item's libraryFiles.

With the library watcher enabled, adding a book folder produces a watcher-scan task (action watcher-scan, libraryId of the library) that finishes successfully and adds the item, without moving libraries.lastScan, which only a full library scan updates.

Setting a library's autoScanCronExpression starts a scheduled scan: without any scan request a library-scan task finishes for the library, libraries.lastScan moves forward and a newly staged book is imported.

A library scan loads every item row once after discovery and processes that snapshot; when it rescans an item whose library files changed, checkLibraryItemData saves the libraryFiles array it loaded, so a write that lands on the same item through another route while the scan runs (here: deleting one audio file of a two-file book) is overwritten by the snapshot - the deleted file is stored again as a library file although it no longer exists, while the media row keeps the live delete's audio file list.

Image library files set the item cover: adding a cover.jpg to an item folder without a cover sets media.coverPath to that file on the next scan, renaming it moves coverPath to the new file and deleting it clears coverPath; audio that gains attached cover art has that art extracted as the item cover.

evidence: go-backend/testmachine/scenarios/scan: 23 upstream scenarios, all passing in two consecutive full packet runs
exceptions: OverDrive MediaMarkers chapters cannot be produced from this pin's ffprobe JSON path (recorded limitation).

The watcher is asserted through its observable effect (a watcher-scan task and the imported item), never through a fixed delay; the packet disables the library watcher for its other file changes so no assertion depends on watcher timing.
Ebook-only items are grouped but not imported: owner-approved compatibility-stub exception (2026-10-30).
Series RSS-feed closure on a removed series is not wired to the Go RSS manager and is not asserted.
